New Relic enabled automatic production log collection by default after an upgrade, increasing billed data ingest unless customers opted out via env vars or account settings.
New Relic's logging agent had a bug that lost a good portion of our logs for months; support was slow to diagnose and unapologetic once the bug was confirmed. We switched to Datadog for logging.
Reminds me of when they intentionally enabled JFR on every single java process. Roughly sextupled our ingest (and associated costs) until we got it shut back off.
When they changed their billing to be per user our bill went up 20x for no additional value... APM hasn't seen a single new feature in the 5 years I have used it.
I run a small environment (~20 small VMs) and we quickly went over the 100GB monthly free plan with just APM Metrics. Support was not helpful in figuring out how to filter irrelevant data.
Used NR for close to 15 years, disappointed with recent direction: removal of development mode/support, worse pricing model, and buggy new UI that keeps regressing.
New Relic is already one of the most expensive items in our budget - our SaaS that monitors our servers is more expensive than the servers themselves.
I love NewRelic, but their pricing always baffled me. When we added QA/UAT/Staging environments, they tried to bill us as if we had 3x as many production environments.

I've long preferred New Relic - it always seemed the most natural to use; important information was easy to find. But had constant problems with metric names exploding, hitting new-metric-name creation locks.
This is the exact same situation my company finds itself in - stuck with New Relic for decent .NET/Java/JS APM metrics in one dashboard, but the new UI is difficult to use and way too bright.

They don’t care that much about open source agent, but they do care about where the server is - there's a huge underserved market for on-premise APMs, and available alternatives aren't nearly as good as New Relic.
I used New Relic for the first time at my current job - while invaluable to our team, the UI is slow and very confusing; I can never remember what button to click, and it loads slowly.
Currently using NR, but it's slow, expensive and the in-cluster collection services are frustratingly fragile.

At $dayjob comparing Azure Application Insights and New Relic: New Relic is useful but too slow in practice, especially outside the US due to trans-oceanic network latency to the cloud-hosted service.
